strength: A sharply defined distraction problem, a shipped product, reported usage and revenue, and a documented RevenueCat lifecycle. Its public MIT repository explains the native bridge and launch fixes.
caveat: Instagram markup changes remain a reliability dependency. Bring the subscription lifecycle, failure recovery and actual messaging experience into the short demo. Reported commercial figures were not independently audited.

strength: Offline tutoring addresses an unusually concrete constraint. Public source includes native model/download infrastructure and RevenueCat purchases. The submission reports budget-device testing and field feedback.
caveat: The sponsorship hook grants local success when no offering is available. That demo fallback is not a verified transaction or proof of a funded student kit. Model-answer accuracy and field outcomes remain unverified here.

strength: Distinctive pottery-and-repair habit design; premium expands the collection instead of charging for recovery. Reviewed source contains real offering, purchase, restore and entitlement paths; MIT license present.
caveat: A student bio and repository suggest potential Next Gen eligibility, but the public page does not explicitly name the track. Successful live purchase execution was not independently reproduced.

strength: A coherent receipt-to-pantry-to-cooking workflow rather than only recipe generation. Reviewed source includes RevenueCat purchase/restore and entitlement handling; MIT license present.
caveat: The submission reports an iPhone Test Store verification, which I did not rerun. Broad feature scope and recipe reliability need a convincing short end-to-end demonstration.

strength: Clear supplier-screening use case, native Mac interface, deterministic core and a sensible single-profile/free versus portfolio/paid boundary. Competition-branch documentation provides unusually detailed purchase and build evidence.
caveat: Customer validation remains a next step. The specialized domain needs a fast, understandable demonstration; extensive engineering documentation alone does not prove user value.

strength: Camera-based form tracking has a clear visual demo. Source contains a native pose module and substantial RevenueCat purchase, restore and account-sync code.
caveat: No root open-source license appeared in the inspected checkout. The supplied tracking screenshot displays 4 FPS, so the zero-lag claim needs measurement. Presence of code is not proof of reliable real-device performance.

strength: Focused task-resumption workflow with checkpoints and a concrete paid boundary. The submission describes showing a real Test Store unlock and restore in a continuous native recording.
caveat: No user-outcome evidence yet. Subscription value versus existing notes/task tools needs justification. Public description reviewed; code and full video not independently audited.

strength: A bounded measurement-to-CAD utility with an understandable paid profile library. Source and committed evidence show actual SDK integration, cancellation/failure handling and a recorded Test Store result.
caveat: Physical printing and caliper validation are explicitly unverified. Correct calculations over authored sample data do not establish practical fit accuracy.

strength: Senior-oriented medication support, large controls, bedside mode and offline storage form a convincing product. Source contains real SDK purchase/restore methods and an MIT license.
caveat: The judge unlock uses a local override that ignores RevenueCat updates. It helps inspect features but cannot establish a successful purchase. Remote caregiver sync is still future work.

strength: Specific study-start barriers, local history and a coherent free/core versus paid/history split. Reviewed source uses official SDK entitlements; the project reports physical-device purchase and restore checks.
caveat: Simpler visual presentation and less novelty than the leading group. The inspected README still describes the entry as a draft; that may be stale, so final submission status is unknown.

strength: Unusual game mechanic turns limited model memory into player-visible consequences. The page describes server-owned state and a successful native Test Store purchase.
caveat: The demo uses a prepared offline script; current live generation is not demonstrated in that recording. Durable server state and physical-device restore remain unresolved.

strength: A narrowly focused reflection journal with local storage, free export and deliberate long-history behavior. RevenueCat gates extended insights and customization.
caveat: The concept is less immediately distinctive than the leading entries. Reported performance and purchase execution were not independently rerun.

strength: Structured calculus practice, mistake review, learning-rule tests and stated Test Store integration make this more credible than a generic AI tutor pitch.
caveat: The page still lists content review, physical-device testing and final demo work as next steps. Public code is linked; category entry is unconfirmed.

strength: Natural-language generation of native widgets is a compelling hook. The page describes native widget bridges and entitlement checks beyond the paywall screen.
caveat: Cross-platform widget behavior needs verification. An obvious drafting artifact remains in the creator bio, reducing presentation quality. Source was linked but not audited.

strength: Combines individually owned notes with a cited class revision guide. Teacher-paid compilations preserve free student participation and give monetization a clear role.
caveat: Student users do not establish student entrants. Native iPad execution and the RevenueCat backend verification are described, not independently tested.

strength: Thoughtful separation of AI signals from deterministic decisions, plus a guardian-funded model. The page discloses limitations instead of presenting a universal safe verdict.
caveat: Reported held-out recall is low, weakening demonstrated effectiveness. Native warning behavior needs testing. The page still contains paste-ready drafting instructions.

strength: A focused logging and environmental-data idea with native Android and a described RevenueCat paywall.
caveat: A cited paper does not validate this app’s predictions or therapeutic claims. OneSignal notifications are listed as future work. Do not rank clinical usefulness from the pitch alone.

strength: Clear local rehearsal workflow and unusually explicit limits on recording analysis. The page reports real Test Store purchase/restore checks.
caveat: Custom scenarios, styles and history are still planned paid features. The silent demo cannot establish useful recorded speech playback. This weakens the demonstrated paid product.

strength: A focused quotes app with local content, speech controls and described device testing.
caveat: Limited differentiation against richer submissions. Test Store execution and code quality were not independently tested.

strength: A small briefing utility with a clear intended purchase boundary.
caveat: Native test build and RevenueCat sandbox testing are next steps in the page. The current description provides less working-product evidence than stronger contenders.

strength: Phone-only development demonstrates resourcefulness and a basic sound-selection workflow.
caveat: Actual AI integration is future work despite AI language in the pitch. Stronger entries better establish differentiated user value and execution.

strength: Study material presented as battles may make a memorable demo.
caveat: The page describes RevenueCat as future architecture. A web-only description also leaves supported-platform evidence unresolved; neither gap is cured by naming RevenueCat in tags.

strength: Emergency support is a meaningful problem area.
caveat: The page explicitly describes mock RevenueCat and simulated subscriptions. Reliability and a licensed public repository are not established by the supplied links.

strength: Styling features could produce an appealing presentation.
caveat: The page explicitly describes local mock RevenueCat transactions. Empty template headings remain, and public licensed source is not established by its links.

strength: A student-built blocker with social accountability and reported paying users. Pricing changes based on conversion are good product-learning evidence.
caveat: No public source repository is linked on the submission page. Could be a serious competitor if the required code and category entry are supplied.

strength: A native reading experience with a carefully described content pipeline and RevenueCat premium study tools.
caveat: High-school status is stated, but no public repository is linked on the submission page. Next Gen eligibility cannot be inferred from student status alone.

strength: Beginner running partners, privacy constraints and an explicit unknown/free/pro subscription model show product and technical thought.
caveat: No public repository link on the submission page. Location/community features need real-world reliability; reported use is not independently audited.

strength: Rules-based study priorities and scope restraint support a coherent product story.
caveat: Repository link and student context do not prove Next Gen entry. Less clear purchase execution evidence than leading candidates.

strength: Exercise-controlled RPG mechanics, local pose processing and content-only monetization could make a strong technical demo.
caveat: Student eligibility and category are unknown. Exercise validation is incomplete by the author’s own account; not all movement types have equivalent evidence.

strength: Tactile focus interaction and different simulated materials align well with design/craft judging; a KMP implementation also offers a sponsor-category angle.
caveat: No student eligibility confirmation. Store accounts and publication are future work, so other-category eligibility needs separate verification.

strength: A quiet shared reading room with a specific social experience, matching paid owner tools and reported organic growth. Good design and growth benchmark.
caveat: Growth and revenue are self-reported and not audited here. The Grand Prize has a revenue-based shortlist, so this is not a prediction that it reaches that shortlist.

strength: Physical match-striking, haptics, flame behavior and environmental scenes give the Design category a concrete interaction to judge.
caveat: Student eligibility unknown; design assessment is based on supplied materials rather than hands-on haptics.

strength: Receipt printing and tearing make ordinary personal data into a distinctive tactile artifact. A useful Design benchmark.
caveat: Student eligibility unknown. Health/privacy and cross-platform behavior were not independently tested.

strength: Dog playdates and giftable collectible titles form a particularly coherent HAMM monetization story; ordinary social use remains free.
caveat: Business results and purchase execution were not audited. Student eligibility unknown.

strength: SQL investigation puzzles, a purpose-built keyboard and case progression provide an assessable Game/Design proposition.
caveat: Puzzle quality needs actual playtesting. No student eligibility established.

strength: Two-device home-care call signaling, acknowledgement and single-tap accessibility provide a specific Peace Prize case.
caveat: The author documents a multi-caregiver acknowledgement issue and range/force-quit limitations. No independent reliability test or student eligibility confirmation.

strength: Two linked shadow constraints create a clear puzzle hook with a bounded paid unlock. Useful Game/Design benchmark.
caveat: The author explicitly lacks independent difficulty validation; broad playtest quality is unresolved.

strength: CAD generation with external rule checks is technically ambitious and the page distinguishes verified from proposed artifacts.
caveat: The demo uses the React interface with a stubbed Tauri shell, and generated fabrication output is not orderable yet. Supported native execution and paid value need confirmation.

strength: On-device composition from personal footage is a memorable design and KMP benchmark, with reported organic distribution.
caveat: The page places RevenueCat paid features in future work, leaving current required integration unclear. Do not mistake a strong concept for verified award eligibility.

strength: Native math practice and a student creator make it relevant to the broader student screen.
caveat: No RevenueCat implementation is explained in the page. AI correctness and current versus planned adaptive features need clearer evidence.

strength: Student-built native study planner with separate familiarity/mastery signals and concrete integration debugging lessons.
caveat: Production billing is future work; that alone is not a Next Gen problem, but successful test purchases and category entry still need evidence.

strength: A narrow local snippet workflow and a usage-limit paywall are understandable.
caveat: The demo unlock is not purchase verification. Drafting artifacts remain in the page, and platform extensions are future work.

strength: Offline multi-hop communications would be valuable if the described native behavior is substantiated.
caveat: No RevenueCat implementation appears in the description. Cross-platform mesh and battery claims require hardware evidence; I did not treat the pitch as verified engineering.
